newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Second Taiwan teen reported kidnapped, killed. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Second Taiwan teen reported kidnapped, killed. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]

text.p: Taiwan police on Tuesday revealed the grisly details of the second kidnapping and murder case on the island in one month, this time of a teenaged boy.

Police said 15-year-old Tsai Chin-hsin was snatched as he bicycled to school on April 21, only two days after the nation was stunned by news of the kidnapping and ransom of Pai Hsiao-yan, the 17-year old daughter of a television celebrity. (Corrects to make clear news was of kidnapping and ransom, not murder.)
The Pai case, the latest in a series of shocking and still unsolved murders, sparked a political firestorm over a perceived breakdown of law and order and demands for a government shake-up.
Tsai, the son of a Taoyuan businessman, was dead even before his kidnappers called his parents to demand a T$3 million (US$108,000) ransom, police in the northern Taiwan county said.
"He was strangled even before the abductors called to demand the ransom," deputy police chief Yao Wu-hsing said.

Investigators said the boy was kidnapped by his father's former employee, identified as Liu Cheng-liang, who said he was poorly treated in the company, and other accomplices. Liu turned himself in on Tuesday, but other suspects remained at large.
Although the case was not made public until Tuesday, Tsai was kidnapped in the midst of the huge public uproar over the similar case of Pai.
Police declined to say whether Tsai's kidnappers were influenced by reports of Pai's abduction.
The boy's father, Tsai Chien-ho, questioned whether it was safe to live in Taiwan, a crowded island of 21 million people.
"The social law and order have deteriorated badly. Is Taiwan still a liveable place?" Tsai asked tearfully.
"I am just a small businessman. I am neither famous nor rich. I don't know why it happened to me," he said.
The Pai case already had aroused deep concern about public safety in Taiwan.

Pai was abducted on her way to school on April 14 and the story broke publicly on the 19th, sparking days of public worry and appeals for her release. The kidnappers severed a finger and sent it to her mother with a demand for US$5 million in ransom.
Taiwan was shocked when police found Pai's body floating naked in a river on April 28.
Police said the kidnappers had strangled Pai, bound her hands and sunk her in the river with weights. Three suspects remain the target of a massive police search.

The crime rekindled anger over investigators' failure to solve the gangland-style murder of Taoyuan's county magistrate and seven others in his home last November or the murder of an opposition leader in southern Taiwan two weeks later.
More than 50,000 people marched in Taipei on May 4 to denounce Pai's murder and rising crime, and to demand Premier Lien Chan's resignation and a cabinet reshuffle.
Civic groups said they planned another mass street march on Sunday in a new show of mounting public discontent.
